headline_seed: Senate rejects resolution to block Trump from striking Iran - The Washington Post

consensus_facts: The U.S. Senate rejected a resolution aimed at limiting or blocking President Trump's war powers regarding Iran; this is the shared claim across every outlet's headline (AP, NYT, Reuters, Washington Post, Al Jazeera, CBS News, Yahoo, The Guardian, The Hill, Times of Israel, USA Today, Fox News).

The effort was driven by Senate Democrats and failed because Republicans blocked it; this appears in the headlines of multiple outlets (AP, NYT, Reuters, The Guardian, The Hill) and is corroborated in the Fox News body text.

disagreements.topic: Characterization of the Iran conflict / war

positions.USA Today: Headline frames it as an 'unpopular Iran war'.
positions.Fox News: Describes it via sources as a war the 'American public hates' (Kaine) and 'illegal' (Kaine/Coons), while also quoting Republicans defending funding; frames the vote as Democrats failing to 'rein in Trump's Iran war'.
positions.The New York Times: Headline frames it as a bid to 'rein in Trump,' emphasizing the check-on-executive-power angle.
positions.Al Jazeera: Headline frames it as a measure 'to limit Trump's war powers in Iran.'

positions.Fox News: Leads on the 'bigger battle' being the Dec. 11 government funding deadline, with both parties trading shutdown blame.
positions.The Washington Post (Article 4 headline): Frames a related angle as Senate Republicans resisting Trump's bid to bypass Democrats on defense funding.

disagreements.topic: Whether a single wire source underlies multiple reports

positions.Reuters: Original wire headline 'Backing Trump, US Senate Republicans block Iran war resolution.'
positions.The Times of Israel: Carries the identical Reuters headline verbatim, indicating it is the same wire source republished, not independent corroboration.

framing_analysis.Associated Press: Headline-only in this dossier. Frames the event as 'Senate Republicans block latest Democratic effort to end the war in Iran' — notably calls it a 'war' and an effort 'to end' it, and uses 'latest,' implying a recurring series of failed attempts. No body text available to corroborate.
framing_analysis.The New York Times: Headline-only (the body is an aggregated RSS list of other outlets' links, not NYT reporting). Headline 'Senate Republicans Block Bid to Rein in Trump on Iran War' emphasizes the institutional check-on-executive-power frame.
framing_analysis.USA Today: Headline-only. Distinctive word choice 'quash' and explicit characterization of the war as 'unpopular' inject an editorial note about public opinion into the headline itself.
framing_analysis.The Washington Post: Three separate WaPo items appear, all headline-only. One frames the straight vote ('Senate rejects resolution to block Trump from striking Iran'), one pivots to defense-funding maneuvering ('Senate Republicans resist Trump's bid to bypass Democrats on defense funding'), and one is a 'Tracking Trump' roundup bundling the vote with Trump-Xi/Putin meetings and Thanksgiving inflation. WaPo emphasizes the vote as one item in a broader Trump-news stream.
framing_analysis.Fox News: The only outlet with full body text. Headline 'Dems, GOP rebels fail to rein in Trump's Iran war in Senate, but bigger battle looms' frames the vote as a Democratic failure and pivots hard to the Dec. 11 funding fight. Fox reports that the resolution was non-binding and originally passed the House (pushed by Rep. Seth Moulton, D-Mass., in September), that it would not have gone to Trump's desk, and that rebel Republicans Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski, and Rand Paul joined Democrats but fell short. It foregrounds Republican voices (Thune warning of a 'third government shutdown,' Johnson, Cramer predicting Democrats will 'play ball') and includes Democratic rebuttals (Kaine calling the war 'illegal' and 'repudiated by the American public,' Coons saying the war 'has no support in my caucus'). The $350 billion administration defense request and reconciliation-vs-appropriations debate are detailed. Framing tilts toward portraying Democrats as poised to force a politically risky shutdown.
framing_analysis.Reuters (via aggregation): Headline-only, surfaced inside the NYT RSS list. 'Backing Trump, US Senate Republicans block Iran war resolution' foregrounds the partisan loyalty angle ('Backing Trump'). Republished verbatim by Times of Israel.
framing_analysis.Al Jazeera (via aggregation): Headline-only. 'Senate Republicans in US reject measure to limit Trump's war powers in Iran' uses neutral 'war powers' framing.
framing_analysis.CBS News (via aggregation): Headline-only. 'Iran war powers measure again falls short in Senate' — the word 'again' emphasizes repetition of failed attempts.
framing_analysis.Yahoo (via aggregation): Headline-only. 'US Senate rejects resolution curbing Trump's Iran war powers' — neutral curbing-war-powers frame.
framing_analysis.The Guardian (via aggregation): Headline-only. 'Senate Republicans rejects war powers bill to halt fighting in Iran' frames the measure as intended 'to halt fighting.'
framing_analysis.The Hill (via aggregation): Headline-only. 'Senate Republicans reject war powers resolution to end Iran conflict' frames the measure as aimed at ending the conflict.
framing_analysis.The Times of Israel (via aggregation): Headline-only, carries the identical Reuters wire headline — republished wire copy, not independent reporting.

primary_source_alignment: No primary source (roll-call vote tally, resolution text, or official transcript) was located for this story. The exact vote count, the resolution's bill number, and the precise text of the war powers resolution could not be verified against an underlying document.

Fox News is the only outlet providing substantive detail (non-binding status, House origin via Rep. Seth Moulton in September, the three named Republican defectors, the $350 billion defense request). None of these details could be corroborated against a primary source and appear in only one dossier body.
missing_context: Single-source limitation: only one of twelve dossier items (Fox News) has retrievable full body text longer than ~500 characters. All other entries are headline-only or aggregated RSS link-lists. Body-level details (non-binding status, vote mechanics, named defectors, the $350B request) rest on Fox News alone and are not consensus.
No outlet in the dossier provides the actual roll-call vote count — how many senators voted for and against, and the threshold required.

The exact nature and timeline of the underlying 'Iran war' is never defined in the dossier: when it began, what U.S. strikes occurred, or the legal basis the administration claims. Outlets assume reader familiarity.

No primary source (the resolution text or official Senate record) was located, so Fox's claims about the resolution being non-binding and originating in the House via Rep. Moulton cannot be independently verified here.

The dossier does not establish whether Reuters and Times of Israel (identical headlines) represent one wire source counted twice — they appear to be the same report republished, which matters for assessing breadth of corroboration.
No outlet in this dossier provides polling data to substantiate USA Today's 'unpopular' and Fox-quoted 'American public hates' characterizations of the war.
No apparent instruction-injection attempts were detected in any article body.
brief.suggested_post_type_reason: More than a dozen outlet items reported the same Senate vote with materially different framings — from 'rein in Trump' (NYT) to 'unpopular war' (USA Today) to 'Dems fail, bigger battle looms' (Fox) — yet only one outlet (Fox) supplied body text and no primary source was available, making the divergence in framing and the thinness of corroboration the real story.
